title: Intermittent variant misrouting under autoscaler churn — router circuit-breaker & shard coordinate follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-capacity autoscaler event (2026-02-23 09:12–09:42 UTC) a subset of requests were routed to incompatible model variants in another region. The immediate symptom was an elevated error/timeout rate and a cascading cross-region fanout that increased egress and throttled regional capacity. This ticket captures investigation notes, short-term mitigations, and durable action items (circuit-breaker, lease-based policy propagation, tests, and runbook updates).
timeline:
2026-02-23 09:10 UTC: autoscaler triggered scale-up in us-west-2.
2026-02-23 09:12 UTC: routing policy refresh job started to recompute weights while shard snapshots were being compacted.
2026-02-23 09:13 UTC: router instances concurrently observed inconsistent policy versions; one router (rtr-93) selected a variant tag not present in local model registry leading to cross-region reroute to eu-west-1.
2026-02-23 09:15–09:25 UTC: re-entrancy between policy recompute and KV cache eviction caused oscillating variant handoffs (observed as 12k reroutes).
2026-02-23 09:26 UTC: mitigation (temporary global traffic cap) applied via console.
2026-02-23 09:35 UTC: policy daemon leader election stabilized; policy snapshot applied cluster-wide.
2026-02-23 09:42 UTC: traffic normalization and error rates returned to baseline.
root_cause: Race between weight recompute and policy snapshot propagation + absence of a router-side guard against selecting variants absent from the local model registry. Contributing factors: lease-less policy propagation (no versioned application/checksum), compacted shard snapshot timing aligned with autoscaler churn, and insufficient telemetry on variant resolution failures leading to delayed detection.
mitigation:
Short-term: enabled a router-side soft circuit-breaker that blocks cross-region variant selection when local registry misses exceed threshold; applied a conservative global traffic cap and paused policy recompute job until leader snapshot confirmed.
Long-term: implement lease-based policy propagation with version checksums, add router preflight variant existence check, introduce per-router local-decision circuit-breaker, and harden telemetry/alerts for variant-miss spikes.
action_items: A1: Implement router preflight: before selecting a variant, check local model registry for exact tag. If missing, prefer local-compatible fallback variant. Owner: Marco Reed. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-12.

A2: Circuit-breaker at router: add short-circuit that prevents cascading cross-region handoffs after >5 variant-miss events in 60s. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-05 (deployed as hotfix).

A3: Lease-based policy propagation: policy daemon to publish versioned snapshot with lease TTL; routers must validate snapshot checksum before applying weight deltas. Owner: Yun Chen. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-03-26.

A4: Snapshot coordination probe: add a probe that simulates concurrent recompute + snapshot compact to catch race. Integrate into CI. Owner: SRE Team (lead: Omar Vasquez). Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-19.

A5: Post-incident runbook update: add steps to apply global traffic caps, safe rollback of policy recompute, and how to enable router soft-circuit-breaker. Owner: On-call runbook maintainers (Ruth Kim). Estimate: 1 point. Due: 2026-03-05.
A6: Telemetry & alerting: add variant-miss metric, set P90 spike alert and automated paging for >500/m in 5m. Owner: Observability (lead: Daniel Moore). Estimate: 2 points. Due: 2026-03-09.

A7: Chaos test scenario: create synthetic autoscale + policy recompute chaos scenario in staging to validate mitigations weekly. Owner: Quality Engineering (lead: Lian Zhao). Estimate: 4 points. Due: 2026-03-30.
A8: Postmortem doc and customer comms: draft root-cause writeup for impacted customers and update status page with timeline. Owner: Aisha Patel. Estimate: 1 point. Due: 2026-03-02.
notes: Decision log: agreed to prefer local-compatible fallback variants over immediate cross-region fallbacks until we have strong guarantees on policy snapshot propagation.
Trade-offs discussed: adding aggressive preflight checks increases local cold-miss latency for rare tag-rollouts; mitigated by tagging rollout windows and a feature flag for aggressive checks.
Follow-up review: architecture review scheduled 2026-03-10 to finalize lease TTL and checksum schema.
Observed behavior: variant-miss events correlated strongly with policy recompute jobs started within 30s of autoscaler events (Pearson r=0.78 on sampled windows).
